extracted.intended_audience: aspiring authors and writers querying literary agents
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and behavioural rules for writers querying agents and developing manuscripts, drawn from a literary agent's blog and reminiscences; includes high-level 'rules for writers' and concrete examples of editorial priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be Prepared! (aka Follow the Damn Directions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Be Prepared! (aka Follow the Damn Directions)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphatic instruction to follow submission directions and be prepared before querying — the blog pairs this motto with other practical query-related resources (Query Letter Help, Query Letter Diagnostics).

rubrics_metrics.name: Be Reachable
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expectations that authors provide reliable contact information and be responsive to agent communications (explicitly listed in the rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Be Tenacious
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinforced by anecdote: “Three rejections are nothing! After we get a hundred rejections we'll talk.” Encourages persistence in submitting despite multiple rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow submission guidelines / 'Follow the Damn Directions'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practically: adhere to an agent's stated submission requirements (formatting, materials requested, method of contact). The blog's repeated admonition frames following directions as a basic professionalism criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persistence in querying
rubrics_metrics.description: Three rejections are nothing! After we get a hundred rejections we'll talk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: Expect many rejections; persistence/tenacity is required. The anecdote is presented as an agent's realistic framing of the submission process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action scenes should create urgency and conflict
rubrics_metrics.description: Make action scenes frantic and urgent (they should be racing against the clock).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example/advice from an author anecdote: Janet advised changing a sedate Central Park action coda into a frantic race 'racing against the clock to survive' — illustrating a criterion for pacing and tension in scenes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Careful word choice and strong vocabulary
rubrics_metrics.description: Be particular about word choice; have a strong vocabulary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple reminiscences note Janet's attention to diction and word choice as a marker of quality; authors benefited when she corrected or suggested better wording.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use editorial feedback to identify and fix problems
rubrics_metrics.description: "I'm not creative. I can't tell you how to fix things. But I can tell you what's wrong."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expectation-setting: an agent/editor may primarily diagnose problems rather than supply creative fixes; writers should be prepared to accept critique and make changes. Authors' testimonials show that following such critiques improved their work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write through the manuscript to discover its core
rubrics_metrics.description: "You just have to write your way through this book to find out what it's really about."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advice encouraging drafting and exploration during writing — the creative process as discovery rather than fully planned in advance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical separation in industry advice
rubrics_metrics.description: Protect a rigorous ethical separation between client work and public advice for writers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The blog notes Janet maintained strict boundaries to avoid conflicts of interest — a professional standard for agents who both represent clients and give public guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value idea-driven nonfiction
rubrics_metrics.description: Appreciation for nonfiction projects driven by ideas even if they might not be commercially lucrative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text notes Janet 'loved non-fiction books, even ones that wouldn't necessarily make a lot of money' — implying a criterion for evaluating projects by strength of idea rather than only commercial prospects.
